provider: Atlassian Confluence Premium via Social Impact (nonprofit) License — unlimited file storage

free_tier.stated: Confluence Premium = 'Unlimited file storage'. Atlassian's Feb 2026 announcement grants eligible nonprofits and social enterprises 100% off Confluence 'Standard or Premium up to 25 users' under the Social Impact License. So a verified nonprofit gets a 25-seat Confluence Premium site with no storage cap, for free.

egress.terms: No egress meter on Confluence attachment downloads — attachments are served from api.media.atlassian.com / the site's CDN with no bandwidth line item in the plan comparison.

tooling: Confluence Cloud REST API v1/v2 (POST /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/child/attachment, GET .../child/attachment, GET /wiki/rest/api/content/{id}/download/attachments/{filename}); community CLI wrappers exist (github.com/nlink-jp/confl-cli, github.com/eddieland/confluence-dl, github.com/justmiles/go-confluence). No rclone backend.
chaining: 'Unlimited' is per Confluence *site*; each site is one org. Multiply by creating many spaces inside one site (unlimited spaces even on Free), and by the number of verified nonprofits. Premium edition also removes the 250 GB Standard ceiling for the same $0 — the licence tier is the multiplier, not the seat count.

limits_note: per-object-cap is the binding constraint: 'The default size limit is 100 MB' per attachment, and Atlassian's own migration doc says the limit 'can be configured for Legacy editor pages, but not for the default editor' (feature request CONFCLOUD-72157 still open). So 20 TB = ~200,000 objects of <=100 MB. request-rate: Atlassian does not publish a Confluence Cloud REST request rate on these pages — unverified; the storage page itself is only refreshed 'every 4 hours'. retention: none published; archiving a page does NOT free storage because Atlassian 'stores all attachments for version history purposes' — deletes are the only way to reclaim.

reliability_note: Free Confluence sites can be deactivated for inactivity (login is the counter). Premium removes the storage cap but not the 100 MB object cap, and archived content is billed forever. Anonymous read of a public space works; anonymous write does not (probed: 200 read, 403 write).
